l1_words.meaning: reading material assigned to be read

pattern_explanation: Several Polish words are spelled almost like English words but come from different roots, so the meanings in the two languages have drifted apart.
false_friend_warning: The Polish word 'lektura' (lektura) looks like 'lecture' but means assigned reading material, not a talk given to an audience. 'Aktualny' (aktualny) looks like 'actual' but means current or up to date. 'Ewentualnie' (ewentualnie) looks like 'eventually' but means possibly or if necessary. 'Sympatyczny' (sympatyczny) looks like 'sympathetic' but means nice or pleasant.
